claim: Ji and colleagues measure that nucleus sampling reaches human-level diversity on Wikipedia and news continuations only at the cost of low coherence.
source: Ji, Ke, Wang, Huang, arXiv:2310.01041v2 (2024); ICLR 2024
quote: achieves better diversity at human-level at the cost of low coherence
modelEra: GPT-2 XL and OPT-6.7B, 2023-2024; register measured: Wikipedia and News domains

claim: Ji and colleagues measure that locally typical decoding gave the highest lexical diversity and the lowest coherence of the methods they compared, which they attribute to its over-weighting of the distribution's long tail.
source: Ji, Ke, Wang, Huang, arXiv:2310.01041v2 (2024); ICLR 2024
quote: lexicality (highest diversity) but severe topic shift (lowest coherence)
modelEra: GPT-2 XL and OPT-6.7B, 2023-2024; register measured: Wikipedia and News domains

claim: Ahmed and Singh state that the greedy heuristics inside current decoding algorithms introduce myopic distortions whose result is homogeneous, repetitive and incoherent sentences.
source: Ahmed, Singh, 'Entropy-Aligned Decoding of LMs for Better Writing and Reasoning', arXiv:2601.01714v1 (2026)
quote: yielding sentences that are homogeneous, repetitive
modelEra: January 2026 preprint; base language model not named in the sections read; register measured: WritingPrompts stories and CNN/DailyMail summaries

claim: Ahmed and Singh describe the existing truncation heuristics as ad hoc and grounded only in empirical observation rather than in a principled target.
quote: these heuristics are often ad hoc, based
modelEra: January 2026 preprint; register: creative writing, summarisation, mathematical reasoning

claim: Ahmed and Singh measure that top-p, top-k and min-p all drift systematically away from the target cross-entropy even with tuned hyperparameters, so the entropy of their sampled text is persistently miscalibrated.
quote: exhibit systematic bias away from the target entropy
modelEra: January 2026 preprint; base model not named in the sections read; register measured: WritingPrompts and CNN/DailyMail

claim: Ahmed and Singh report a win rate of 0 per cent for plain temperature sampling at tau equals 1.5 against min-p on the WritingPrompts story task, judged by ChatGPT-5 and averaged over ten seeds.
modelEra: January 2026; judge is ChatGPT-5, not human raters; register measured: WritingPrompts story generation

claim: Chang and colleagues state the nucleus sampling trade-off as a direct one, in which raising the p threshold raises diversity and lowers factuality.
source: Chang, Peng, Bansal, Ramakrishna, Chung, 'REAL Sampling', arXiv:2406.07735v1 (2024)
quote: higher p threshold in the nucleus (top-p) sampling increases the diversity but
modelEra: 7B language models with a 70M forecasting model, June 2024; register measured: FactualityPrompts open-ended continuations

claim: Renze and Guven found no statistically significant effect of sampling temperature between 0.0 and 1.0 on multiple-choice problem-solving accuracy.
source: Renze, Guven, 'The Effect of Sampling Temperature on Problem Solving in Large Language Models', arXiv:2402.05201v3 (2024)
quote: do not have a statistically significant impact on LLM performance
modelEra: nine LLMs, temperatures 0.0 to 1.6, observation 2024; register measured: multiple-choice question answering, not prose

claim: Renze and Guven's temperature result rests on nine language models crossed with five prompt-engineering techniques on a multiple-choice exam sampled from standard benchmarks.
quote: nine popular LLMs with five prompt-engineering techniques
modelEra: nine LLMs, 2024; register measured: multiple-choice question answering

claim: Ilinykh and Dobnik measure that human image captions carry roughly twice the surprisal variance of five vision-and-language model caption sets when scored with a caption-trained n-gram model.
source: Ilinykh, Dobnik, 'Surprisal reveals diversity gaps in image captioning', arXiv:2511.04754v1 (2025)
quote: roughly twice the surprisal variance of models
modelEra: five vision-and-language LLMs with greedy and nucleus decoding, November 2025; register measured: MSCOCO image captions, not prose fiction or archival text

claim: Ilinykh and Dobnik report that rescoring the same captions with a general language model instead of a caption-trained one reverses the human-model surprisal-variance gap, so a single scorer can invert the conclusion.
quote: on a single scorer can completely invert
modelEra: five vision-and-language LLMs, November 2025; register measured: MSCOCO image captions

claim: Xu and colleagues measure that as a loop sets in the minimum Kullback-Leibler divergence between the current step's distribution and the earlier steps' distributions falls towards zero, where a human continuation keeps it away from zero.
source: Xu, Zhou, Celikyilmaz, Ma, 'Look-back Decoding for Open-Ended Text Generation', arXiv:2305.13477v2 (2023)
quote: distribution distance with past gradually approaches 0
modelEra: GPT2-XL and GPT-3 (ada-001, davinci-002), observation 2023; register measured: open-ended continuation and story generation

claim: Xu and colleagues report that the coherence hypothesis behind confidence-following decoders does not always hold, since a greedy decoder rigorously following model confidence can produce incoherent sentences.
quote: coherence hypothesis of pretrained LMs in prior
page: Section 3, discussion of the Table 1 degeneration examples
modelEra: GPT2-XL and GPT-3 ada-001 and davinci-002, 2023; register measured: open-ended continuation

claim: Xu and colleagues relay the induction-head account of Olsson and colleagues, prefix matching and copying, as a possible explanation of repetitive generation.

modelEra: OPT models from 125M to 30B parameters, observation May 2023; register measured: 10,000 English Wikipedia items plus OpenWebText prefixes
